title: Compose explicit Companion invocation in the PWA

gates.name: companion_invocation_browser
gates.command: cd frontend && npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/companion-invocation.spec.ts

verify: Independent invocation verification covers exact explicit POST, success/duplicate/non-governable shapes, zero-call GET/refresh, role/archive denial, request-field exclusion, and unbound production zero-fallback/network behavior.
evidence_required: FT-016-AC-030 RED: no browser explicit Companion run consumer exists; GREEN: only the exact POST reaches the provider-neutral runtime with valid success/duplicate/non-governable presentation, GET/refresh emits zero call, denied/archive paths do not invoke, and production-unbound fails before network I/O without fake fallback; decisive comparison: request allowlist, DOM, provider spy, and unbound network spy; artifact: invocation evidence under .tasks/TASK-107-T3-FT-016-W3/.
purpose: Expose explicit Companion invocation independently of reads, proposal decision, and issue close.
success_outcome: Authorized Boss/Engineer users can invoke only the exact provider-neutral run action while refresh/GET/UI text never triggers it and denied/archive/unbound paths remain safe without fallback.
anti_goals: Do not implement Issue reads, proposal decision, issue close, arbitrary prompt/chat input, automatic triggers, or provider selection.
Do not read browser/CLI/IDE credentials or add a production fake/canned fallback.

forbidden_scope: external provider/network/credential access or production fallback
stop_conditions: The UI needs fields or triggers outside the exact Companion run contract.
The proof requires external provider access, credential discovery, or production fallback.

constraints: Primary owner is Operator PWA; Companion Governance/Runtime owns input, model call, classification, persistence, and response.
Use only the strict run request and test-only deterministic fake/spy setup.
invariants: Only explicit authorized POST can invoke Companion; GET/refresh/events never do.
Production remains unbound and fails closed before network I/O without fake/canned fallback.
verification_targets: FT-016-AC-030: explicit run success/duplicate/non-governable paths, zero-call GET/refresh, role/archive denial, and strict field exclusion.
FT-016-AC-030 T3 harm proof uses isolated issues and proves production-unbound zero-network/no-fallback behavior with safe rerun.
